docstring:
If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$
references: [ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, Filter.liminf (fun n => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(Erdos890.omegaGt k (n + i))) Filter.atTop ≤ ↑k
